title: Codex uninstall and backup: managed outputs removed cleanly, user content untouched
prerequisites: Node.js >= 18 and the make-docs CLI built from this repository.
A fresh disposable fixture workspace; the scenario never touches a maintainer working tree. This scenario owns the PRD 36 R-PROV-2 cleanliness proof at the real-harness layer.

steps.notes: Disposable fixture workspace (workspacePolicy); all later steps run inside it.

steps.run: mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/docs/assets/playbooks/agent" && cp conformance/fixtures/agent/conformance-skill-probe.playbook.md "$WORKSPACE/docs/assets/playbooks/agent/" && printf 'user-authored sentinel\n' > "$WORKSPACE/docs/assets/playbooks/agent/user-authored-note.md" && printf 'user-authored sentinel\n' > "$WORKSPACE/USER-NOTES.md"
steps.notes: User-authored sentinel files sit beside and inside directories the packaging writers manage, so deletion or orphaning is detectable.

steps.run: cd "$WORKSPACE" && make-docs run package ship --harness codex --output-kind plugin --surface native --scope project --package-id conformance-plugin-probe --json agent/conformance-skill-probe
cd "$WORKSPACE" && make-docs run package ship --harness codex --output-kind skills-bundle --surface native --scope project --package-id conformance-skill-probe --json agent/conformance-skill-probe
steps.notes: Both container kinds are installed so uninstall cleanliness is proven across the plugin tree, the skills bundle, and their exposure links in one workspace.

steps.run: cd "$WORKSPACE" && git add -A && git -c user.email=probe@example.invalid -c user.name=probe commit -m baseline
steps.notes: The committed baseline makes the post-uninstall user-content diff byte-exact.

steps.action: Launch Codex inside the workspace and confirm both generated outputs appear in Codex's listing surfaces.
In a fresh Codex thread, invoke the bundled probe skill once, confirming the installed outputs are live before removal.

steps.notes: The backup half of the R-PROV-2 cleanliness pair.

steps.assert: The backup snapshot exists under the workspace backup location, captures the managed state, and did not move, rewrite, or delete any user-authored file.

After removal every managed generated output is gone — the plugin tree, the skills bundle, exposure links, and the generated marketplace entry — and no empty managed directory is orphaned under .codex/plugins/, .agents/, or the skills roots.

git status against the committed baseline shows the user-authored sentinel files (USER-NOTES.md and docs/assets/playbooks/agent/user-authored-note.md) and the fixture Playbook byte-identical: uninstall and backup deleted no user-authored file.

expectedEvidence: Two --json ship transcripts recording the installed plugin and skills bundle (install).
Both outputs visible in Codex's listing surfaces (discover).
A fresh-thread invocation transcript proving the outputs were live before removal (invoke).

Non-TTY backup and removal transcripts plus a git diff against the committed baseline proving managed outputs removed, no orphaned empty managed directories, and user-authored files byte-identical (uninstall).
Model, provider, and runtime captured as run metadata in the result record.

install: Both ship commands exit 0 with --json transcripts recording the generated plugin tree and skills bundle with their ownership records.
discover: Both generated outputs appear in Codex's own listing surfaces for the workspace.
invoke: A fresh Codex thread invokes the bundled probe skill before removal, proving the outputs under test were live.
uninstall: make-docs setup backup snapshots the managed state without touching user-authored files.
make-docs setup remove --backup removes every managed generated output without orphaning an empty managed directory.
The git diff against the committed baseline shows all user-authored sentinel files byte-identical (PRD 36 R-PROV-2).

preconditions.description: The Codex CLI is installed and on PATH.
The Codex CLI is signed in with a working account.
Outbound network access for the harness is available; attested by the operator at run time because probing it would spend it.
The harness can route to a model for the invoke stage; attested by the operator at run time.
